  "core_problem": "Vision-language models answering chart questions cannot reliably map pixel positions to axis values — a deficit that persists even in the largest proprietary models.   "approach": "We propose Axis-Coordinate Calibrated Training (ACCT), a two-stage pipeline that injects explicit pixel↔value supervision into a VLM using programmatic ground truth from synthetic chart renderers, then extends this signal to real charts via bootstrapped calibration. We use Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct as the backbone throughout both training stages (the Instruct variant, not Thinking, to make GRPO rollout compute predictable; see Stage 2 for justification). No 32B comparison is attempted; we stay within the 16-day/200 H100-hour constraint.\n\n**Stage 1 — Coordinate-Calibration LoRA SFT (Days 1–2, ~35–40 H100 hours, unattended overnight run):** We synthesize 50K charts using matplotlib/plotly (CPU, Day 1, ~6–8 hours), extracting programmatic pixel↔value transforms for every tick and data point. The Stage 1 LoRA training job is submitted as an unattended overnight run at the end of Day 1 and completes by Day 2 morning (~35–40 H100 hours on one or two H100s in parallel). Coordinate tasks are constructed in normalized form — e.g., 'at what normalized y-position [0.0–1.0] within the chart plot area does value 7.3 appear?' — to decouple supervision from Qwen3-VL's effective spatial resolution (14×14px patches at 448px input, yielding ~32 vertical bins). Normalization is defined relative to the chart plot area (excluding title/margin), which is available exactly from matplotlib's ax.get_position() in Stage 1 and approximated via RANSAC in Stage 2. Bins of width 0.07 (≈32px) span 2–4 typical tick intervals, providing sufficient discriminative resolution while staying within the model's localization granularity. We fine-tune Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct with LoRA (rank=64, α=128) on these tasks.\n\n**Day 2 Tick Detection Pilot (go/no-go gate for Stage 2 coordinate reward):** After reading Stage 1 results (Day 2 morning), we validate tick-label detection quality on 500 held-out ChartQA real charts using the following concrete pipeline: (i) Prompt Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct with the exact template: 'Identify all y-axis tick labels in this chart. For each visible numeric label along the left vertical axis, output one line in the format — tick_value: <number> | bbox: <|box_start|>(x_min,y_min),(x_max,y_max)<|box_end|> — using Qwen3-VL normalized coordinates (0–1000 scale). If no tick labels are visible, output NO_TICKS_FOUND.' (ii) Parse bounding boxes and numerical values; filter for plausible y-axis positions (x_min < 0.25 of image width). (iii) If ≥3 ticks are detected per chart, run RANSAC linear fit (tick_center_normalized_y → numerical value). (iv) Measure: (a) fraction of 500 charts with ≥3 reliable ticks detected, (b) RANSAC residual distribution (median, 90th percentile). Go/no-go criterion: if VLM grounding achieves ≥60% chart success rate with median RANSAC residual ≤0.06, proceed as designed. If success rate is 40–60%, switch to a dedicated OCR fallback (PaddleOCR-VL for text bounding boxes, then filter numerics by position). If success rate falls below 40% even with PaddleOCR, drop the coordinate reward component entirely from Stage 2 and run answer-reward-only GRPO; report this as an ablation finding rather than a system failure. The tick detection pilot runs in parallel with paper writing on Day 2 and results are reviewed in the Day 3 human gate before Stage 2 begins.\n\n**Stage 2 — GRPO with Composite Reward (Days 3–10, ~90 H100 hours, unattended run):** We apply GRPO on ChartQA training split (~28K examples: ~18.5K augmented + ~9.6K human-written; the same corpus used by BigCharts-R1 for chart RL) with a two-component reward. Stage 2 is submitted as an unattended run beginning Day 3 evening, completing by Day 10. ChartMuseum has no training split — its dev set (162 samples) and test set (1,000 samples) are held out entirely for evaluation. We optionally supplement with 1K samples from PlotQA/DVQA/FigureQA (following BigCharts-R1) for chart-type diversity.\n\n**Backbone and generation cap:** Stage 2 uses Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (not the Thinking variant). The Thinking variant generates 2K–10K token chain-of-thought prefixes per rollout; at 8 rollouts per prompt × 28K prompts, this would require 400+ H100 hours — exceeding our budget. The Instruct variant with max_new_tokens=512 (covering the ACT prefix + answer in all observed cases during Stage 1) caps compute to ~90 H100 hours.\n\n(A) Answer accuracy reward: exact-match or relaxed numeric match (≤5% relative error) as in Chart-RL and BigCharts-R1. (B) Coordinate proximity reward on real charts via bootstrapped calibration (contingent on Day 2 pilot success): (i) detect tick-label bounding boxes using the validated approach from the Day 2 pilot (Qwen3-VL grounding or PaddleOCR fallback); (ii) OCR the numerical value in each detected box; (iii) fit a RANSAC robust linear model mapping detected tick-center normalized-y → numerical value within the chart plot area; (iv) invert to get approximate ground-truth normalized coordinates for queried values. The proximity reward is r = exp(−d²/(2σ²)) in normalized space, where σ is calibrated to 1.5× the median RANSAC residual measured in the Day 2 pilot. When fewer than 3 tick labels are reliably detected on a given chart, the coordinate component is dropped and only the answer reward is used for that example.\n\n**Axis-Calibration Tokens (ACTs):** Before any answer, the model is trained to output a structured prefix mapping N tick labels to their normalized positions (relative to the chart plot area): '<ACT> tick_1: value=0 → pos=0.00; tick_2: value=50 → pos=0.47; tick_3: value=100 → pos=1.00 </ACT>'. This forces an explicit spatial intermediate step verifiable against rendering ground truth in Stage 1 and against bootstrapped calibrations in Stage 2. ACTs are strictly more precise than ChartPoint's region-presence bounding boxes and orthogonal to Chart-RL's answer-only GRPO rewards.\n\n**Differentiation from CogAlign:** CogAlign trains invariance of perceptual properties via DPO on transformation pairs; its text-decoder bottleneck insight motivates a perceptual retraining approach. ACCT targets a complementary and distinct failure: the model cannot read off a specific quantity from a specific spatial position even when the chart is not transformed. The two approaches address complementary dimensions of visual arithmetic failures: CogAlign for perceptual invariance, ACCT for calibrated spatial localization.\n\n**Differentiation from Chart-R1:** Chart-R1 (arXiv:2507.15509) applies SFT+GRPO on Qwen2.5-VL-7B with accuracy and format rewards, achieving 34.8% overall on ChartMuseum. ACCT uses a stronger backbone (Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, which already starts at 40.0% overall), adds Stage 1 coordinate-calibration SFT (absent from Chart-R1), and introduces the coordinate proximity reward in Stage 2 GRPO — directly targeting the axis-localization failure that Chart-R1, BigCharts-R1, and all existing methods leave unaddressed.\n\n**Expected improvement range:** We target a 10–20pp gain on ChartMuseum visual tasks (from the Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct baseline of 27.8% to 38–48% visual accuracy), with 15pp as our central estimate. Three reference points calibrate this range: (1) Scale alone cannot close the gap: Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Thinking achieves 38.8% visual using 4× more parameters and extended thinking — targeted coordinate training on an 8B Instruct model should reach comparable or higher visual accuracy by directly addressing the localization deficit rather than increasing compute. (2) Chart-R1 reaches 34.8% overall on ChartMuseum (vs our 40.0% overall baseline) using a weaker backbone and no coordinate supervision; ACCT adds the missing signal on a stronger base, enabling gains beyond what accuracy-reward GRPO alone can provide. (3) The 42.2pp visual-textual gap is structural: dense synthetic-renderer supervision provides exact pixel↔value ground truth for the precise capability ChartMuseum visual tasks test — a training signal entirely absent from all prior work — enabling closure that accuracy-only rewards cannot achieve. A 15pp visual gain (27.8% → 43.0%) would close approximately 35% of the structural visual-textual gap and place ACCT above all ≤10B models currently on the ChartMuseum leaderboard on the visual-reasoning dimension.",

## Reviewer feedback (round 4)
Issues: ["IMPORTANT — Improvement estimate not calibrated against closest comparable evidence: The 'central estimate 15pp' is calibrated against Qwen3-VL-30B scale gains and Chart-R1 accuracy-only GRPO, but not against ChartPoint, which is the closest architectural analog (coordinate-type SFT supervision for chart VLMs) and achieves only +5% on ChartBench. Even though ACCT's value-coordinate supervision is more precise than bounding boxes, claiming 3× the gain requires either: (a) an explicit argument for why axis-value precision unlocks substantially more than region-presence, or (b) a lower central estimate (e.g., 8–12pp) with 15pp as the optimistic upper bound. Without this, EMNLP reviewers will flag the improvement estimate as unsubstantiated.", "IMPORTANT — Catastrophic forgetting from Stage 1 LoRA SFT unacknowledged: Stage 1 fine-tunes Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct on 50K synthetic coordinate-prediction tasks in normalized [0,1] space — a distribution very different from natural ChartQA / ChartMuseum questions. Even with LoRA, this induces a prior that Stage 2 GRPO must overcome. The ablation 'Stage 1 only vs full ACCT' will surface this, but if Stage 1 hurts performance on textual or synthesis questions, the paper's contribution narrative could collapse. An 8B model with coordinate training is removing both advantages and adding one different one; there is no strong prior that this trade is favorable for visual accuracy specifically. Soften to 'suggests the visual ceiling for 8B models with targeted supervision may approach 38–40%' rather than 'should reach comparable or higher.'"]
Feedback: All previous blocking issues (Rounds 1–3) are resolved. The proposal is now well-structured, technically concrete, and has verified leaderboard numbers, confirmed paper references, and a plausible EMNLP timeline. Two important remaining issues need targeted fixes:

**Fix 1 (Important — Calibrate the improvement estimate against ChartPoint):** Add one paragraph comparing ACCT's expected gains to ChartPoint's +5% on ChartBench. Explain why axis-value coordinate calibration should yield substantially larger gains than region-presence bounding boxes: the specific failure mode ChartMuseum visual tasks test is exactly 'map pixel position to axis value,' which region-presence bounding boxes cannot teach but normalized coordinate prediction directly addresses. If this argument is compelling, the 10–20pp range can stand; if not, shift the central estimate to 8–12pp and present 15pp as the optimistic scenario. This single paragraph will pre-empt the most predictable EMNLP reviewer objection.

**Fix 2 (Important — Add catastrophic forgetting check to Day 3 gate):** Amend the Day 3 human gate (Human gate A) to include a mandatory ChartQA validation accuracy check on a 500-sample subset, in addition to coordinate prediction error. Based on the literature search, here's a concise summary addressing the reviewer's catastrophic forgetting concern:

## Key Findings on LoRA Forgetting Severity

**Forgetting is real but controlled**: Research shows LoRA exhibits a learning-forgetting trade-off—higher ranks (like 64–128) improve task plasticity but increase forgetting compared to full fine-tuning. However, LoRA substantially *mitigates* forgetting compared to full fine-tuning on unrelated tasks, making it more stable for continual learning scenarios.

**VLM-specific solutions exist**: Recent work on vision-language models directly addresses your use case:
- **Comp-LoRA** (Complementary Subspace LoRA) reduces forgetting by optimizing in the complementary subspace to preserve vision-language alignment while learning novel tasks
- **SMoLoRA** uses separable routing to prevent task interference in continual VLM tuning
- **Model merging** shows greater robustness to forgetting than single LoRA modules

## Standard Forgetting Detection Practices

The literature identifies early mechanistic signatures before behavioral collapse:
- **Landscape flattening** precedes forgetting by 1–2 epochs; curvature metrics (Hessian eigenvalues) decrease first, then accuracy drops
- **Task vector overlap** with pre-trained parameters is a quantifiable CF metric
- These enable detection before catastrophic performance loss occurs

Mitigation approaches during training:
- Curvature regularization (34% forgetting reduction with ~12% slower convergence)
- Loss landscape flattening via sharpness-aware minimization
- Element-wise parameter importance regularization

## Stage 2 GRPO Recovery Capacity

**Critical finding**: Research on two-stage SFT→RL pipelines shows that RL functions as **memory restoration, not capability creation**. The recovery ability has hard limits:
- If Stage 1 SFT is excessive, Stage 2 RL cannot fully recover lost base model competencies
- OOD performance degradation/recovery correlates with singular vector rotations (extremal spectral components), not magnitude changes
- **DeepSeek-R1's approach**: Use brief SFT to stabilize, then apply GRPO—this is validated in practice

For your 50K→28K pipeline, the risk is real if Stage 1 is too aggressive, but GRPO can partially recover if the distribution shift isn't extreme. Detection via early curvature monitoring (before accuracy drops) is recommended.

  "approach": "We propose Axis-Coordinate Calibrated Training (ACCT), a two-stage pipeline that injects explicit pixel↔value supervision into a VLM using programmatic ground truth from synthetic chart renderers, then extends this signal to real charts via bootstrapped calibration. We use Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct as the backbone throughout both training stages (the Instruct variant, not Thinking, to make GRPO rollout compute predictable; see Stage 2 for justification). No 32B comparison is attempted; we stay within the 16-day/200 H100-hour constraint.

**Stage 1 — Coordinate-Calibration LoRA SFT (Days 1–2, ~35–40 H100 hours, unattended overnight run):** We synthesize 50K charts using matplotlib/plotly (CPU, Day 1, ~6–8 hours), extracting programmatic pixel↔value transforms for every tick and data point. The Stage 1 LoRA training job is submitted as an unattended overnight run at the end of Day 1 and completes by Day 2 morning (~35–40 H100 hours on one or two H100s in parallel). Coordinate tasks are constructed in normalized form — e.g., 'at what normalized y-position [0.0–1.0] within the chart plot area does value 7.3 appear?' — to decouple supervision from Qwen3-VL's effective spatial resolution (14×14px patches at 448px input, yielding ~32 vertical bins). Normalization is defined relative to the chart plot area (excluding title/margin), which is available exactly from matplotlib's ax.get_position() in Stage 1 and approximated via RANSAC in Stage 2. Bins of width 0.07 (≈32px) span 2–4 typical tick intervals, providing sufficient discriminative resolution while staying within the model's localization granularity. We fine-tune Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct with LoRA (rank=64, α=128) on these tasks.

**Day 2 Tick Detection Pilot (go/no-go gate for Stage 2 coordinate reward):** After reading Stage 1 results (Day 2 morning), we validate tick-label detection quality on 500 held-out ChartQA real charts using the following concrete pipeline: (i) Prompt Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct with the exact template: 'Identify all y-axis tick labels in this chart. For each visible numeric label along the left vertical axis, output one line in the format — tick_value: <number> | bbox: <|box_start|>(x_min,y_min),(x_max,y_max)<|box_end|> — using Qwen3-VL normalized coordinates (0–1000 scale). If no tick labels are visible, output NO_TICKS_FOUND.' (ii) Parse bounding boxes and numerical values; filter for plausible y-axis positions (x_min < 0.25 of image width). (iii) If ≥3 ticks are detected per chart, run RANSAC linear fit (tick_center_normalized_y → numerical value). (iv) Measure: (a) fraction of 500 charts with ≥3 reliable ticks detected, (b) RANSAC residual distribution (median, 90th percentile). Go/no-go criterion: if VLM grounding achieves ≥60% chart success rate with median RANSAC residual ≤0.06, proceed as designed. If success rate is 40–60%, switch to a dedicated OCR fallback (PaddleOCR-VL for text bounding boxes, then filter numerics by position). If success rate falls below 40% even with PaddleOCR, drop the coordinate reward component entirely from Stage 2 and run answer-reward-only GRPO; report this as an ablation finding rather than a system failure. The tick detection pilot runs in parallel with paper writing on Day 2 and results are reviewed in the Day 3 human gate before Stage 2 begins.

**Stage 2 — GRPO with Composite Reward (Days 3–10, ~90 H100 hours, unattended run):** We apply GRPO on ChartQA training split (~28K examples: ~18.5K augmented + ~9.6K human-written; the same corpus used by BigCharts-R1 for chart RL) with a two-component reward. Stage 2 is submitted as an unattended run beginning Day 3 evening, completing by Day 10. ChartMuseum has no training split — its dev set (162 samples) and test set (1,000 samples) are held out entirely for evaluation. We optionally supplement with 1K samples from PlotQA/DVQA/FigureQA (following BigCharts-R1) for chart-type diversity.

**Backbone and generation cap:** Stage 2 uses Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct (not the Thinking variant). The Thinking variant generates 2K–10K token chain-of-thought prefixes per rollout; at 8 rollouts per prompt × 28K prompts, this would require 400+ H100 hours — exceeding our budget. The Instruct variant with max_new_tokens=512 (covering the ACT prefix + answer in all observed cases during Stage 1) caps compute to ~90 H100 hours.

(A) Answer accuracy reward: exact-match or relaxed numeric match (≤5% relative error) as in Chart-RL and BigCharts-R1. (B) Coordinate proximity reward on real charts via bootstrapped calibration (contingent on Day 2 pilot success): (i) detect tick-label bounding boxes using the validated approach from the Day 2 pilot (Qwen3-VL grounding or PaddleOCR fallback); (ii) OCR the numerical value in each detected box; (iii) fit a RANSAC robust linear model mapping detected tick-center normalized-y → numerical value within the chart plot area; (iv) invert to get approximate ground-truth normalized coordinates for queried values. The proximity reward is r = exp(−d²/(2σ²)) in normalized space, where σ is calibrated to 1.5× the median RANSAC residual measured in the Day 2 pilot. When fewer than 3 tick labels are reliably detected on a given chart, the coordinate component is dropped and only the answer reward is used for that example.

**Axis-Calibration Tokens (ACTs):** Before any answer, the model is trained to output a structured prefix mapping N tick labels to their normalized positions (relative to the chart plot area): '<ACT> tick_1: value=0 → pos=0.00; tick_2: value=50 → pos=0.47; tick_3: value=100 → pos=1.00 </ACT>'. This forces an explicit spatial intermediate step verifiable against rendering ground truth in Stage 1 and against bootstrapped calibrations in Stage 2. ACTs are strictly more precise than ChartPoint's region-presence bounding boxes and orthogonal to Chart-RL's answer-only GRPO rewards.

**Differentiation from CogAlign:** CogAlign trains invariance of perceptual properties via DPO on transformation pairs; its text-decoder bottleneck insight motivates a perceptual retraining approach. ACCT targets a complementary and distinct failure: the model cannot read off a specific quantity from a specific spatial position even when the chart is not transformed. The two approaches address complementary dimensions of visual arithmetic failures: CogAlign for perceptual invariance, ACCT for calibrated spatial localization.

**Differentiation from Chart-R1:** Chart-R1 (arXiv:2507.15509) applies SFT+GRPO on Qwen2.5-VL-7B with accuracy and format rewards, achieving 34.8% overall on ChartMuseum. ACCT uses a stronger backbone (Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct, which already starts at 40.0% overall), adds Stage 1 coordinate-calibration SFT (absent from Chart-R1), and introduces the coordinate proximity reward in Stage 2 GRPO — directly targeting the axis-localization failure that Chart-R1, BigCharts-R1, and all existing methods leave unaddressed.

**Calibration against ChartPoint:** The closest architectural analog is ChartPoint (ICCV 2025), which achieves +5% on ChartBench (60.91% → 65.95%) by training models to attend to chart regions via bounding-box SFT with PointCoT reflection — a spatial attention signal that teaches *where to attend in the image*. ACCT's supervision is qualitatively distinct: it trains the model to output a specific numerical axis value for a given normalized pixel position, which is the exact inverse mapping ChartMuseum visual tasks require. ChartMuseum's visual reasoning category explicitly includes 'X/Y Value Identification' questions — tasks where the correct answer requires converting a pixel position to an axis value — a capability that region-presence bounding-box supervision cannot directly impart but normalized coordinate regression targets directly. Two additional factors support a larger effect than ChartPoint's +5%: (1) ChartPoint's gain is measured over ChartBench's full mixed corpus of 600K+ auto-generated QA pairs spanning text-adjacent and arithmetic tasks where bounding-box grounding yields minimal benefit, diluting gains attributable to spatial attention alone; ACCT is evaluated on ChartMuseum visual tasks specifically, a benchmark engineered to isolate the axis-localization deficit. (2) ChartPoint's bounding-box signal is binary (region present/absent); ACCT's continuous normalized regression provides a dense, differentiable gradient over exact value-position correspondences, delivering richer supervision per example. Together, these distinctions — supervision precision (continuous value-coordinate regression vs. binary region-presence), training-evaluation alignment (axis-value identification vs. mixed QA), and evaluation sensitivity (visual-only isolation vs. aggregate score) — justify 8–15pp on ChartMuseum visual tasks as the plausible range corresponding to ACCT's qualitative improvement over ChartPoint's signal. The central estimate of 10–12pp is the conservative reading; 15pp is the optimistic scenario if coordinate calibration generalizes efficiently across chart styles.

**Expected improvement range:** We target an 8–15pp gain on ChartMuseum visual tasks (from the Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct baseline of 27.8% to 36–43% visual accuracy), with 10–12pp as our central estimate. Four reference points calibrate this range: (1) Scale and reasoning alone cannot close the gap: Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Thinking reaches 38.8% visual using 4× more parameters and extended thinking; the persistence of this deficit across scale suggests the bottleneck is training signal rather than model capacity, and targeted coordinate supervision on an 8B Instruct model may bring visual accuracy into the range achieved by the 30B Thinking model — though this trade (scale and extended thinking replaced by coordinate calibration) has no direct empirical precedent, so 38–40% visual is a reference range rather than a guaranteed floor. (2) Chart-R1 reaches 34.8% overall on ChartMuseum (vs our 40.0% overall baseline) using a weaker backbone and no coordinate supervision; ACCT adds the missing signal on a stronger base, enabling gains beyond what accuracy-reward GRPO alone can provide. (3) The 42.2pp visual-textual gap is structural: dense synthetic-renderer supervision provides exact pixel↔value ground truth for the precise capability ChartMuseum visual tasks test — a training signal entirely absent from all prior work — enabling targeted closure that accuracy-only rewards cannot achieve. (4) Calibration against ChartPoint: ACCT's normalized coordinate regression is a precision upgrade over ChartPoint's bounding-box region-presence supervision, applied to a more sensitive evaluation; 8–15pp corresponds to ACCT's training-evaluation alignment advantage over ChartPoint's +5% on ChartBench. A 10–12pp visual gain (27.8% → 38–40%) would match or exceed the visual accuracy of the 30B Thinking model (38.8% visual) while using a 4× smaller model without extended thinking, validating that training signal is the primary bottleneck for axis localization; it places ACCT above all current ≤10B leaderboard entries on the visual reasoning dimension and closes approximately 23–28% of the structural visual-textual gap.",
